terms.gloss: agricultural, of farming and the country
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.69: rēs rūstica (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the country as against the town (the opposite of urbānus), and so of farming: rēs rūstica is agriculture, the subject of Varro’s Rērum rūsticārum librī and Columella’s Dē rē rūsticā. Of a person it can also mean boorish, unpolished.
Also written as one word, agricultūra; Cato’s book is Dē agrī cultūrā.

terms.gloss: of land; of the distribution of public land
terms.comment: Classically a legal and political word, of land laws (lēgēs agrāriae), not of farming in general.

phrases.latin: nam rēs rūstica sīc est, sī ūnam rem sērō fēceris, omnia opera sērō faciēs
phrases.english: for farming is like this: if you do one thing late, you’ll do every job late

sources: Lewis & Short: rusticus · Lewis & Short: cultura · Lewis & Short: agrarius
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato, loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.
